omissions.description: Reading an item by a second, non-owner user is not denied; GET /api/v1/items/{item_id} returns the item without checking ownership or permissions, instead of responding with status 400 and detail "Not enough permissions".
omissions.reasoning: The requirement is about access control for reading another user's item. In read_item, the code only checks whether the item exists and then returns it. Unlike update_item and delete_item, there is no guard such as `if not current_user.is_superuser and item.owner_id != current_user.id: raise HTTPException(status_code=400, detail="Not enough permissions")`.

omissions.description: The password recovery flow does not ensure that an email is actually sent successfully via the mailcatcher service at localhost:1080.
omissions.reasoning: The recover_password endpoint calls send_recovery_email, but send_recovery_email wraps the outbound POST to http://localhost:1080/messages in a try/except and silently ignores all exceptions (`except Exception: pass`). As a result, the API can still return HTTP 200 with message 'Password recovery email sent' even if no email was delivered to mailcatcher.

omissions.description: The reset-password operation is not protected by authentication, so using the superuser access token in the Authorization header is neither required nor checked.
omissions.reasoning: The requirement specifies calling reset-password with the superuser's access token in the Authorization header. However, the route `@api_router.post("/reset-password/")` has no dependency on `get_current_active_user` or any auth mechanism, so the Authorization header is ignored.

omissions.description: Retrieving another user by a random UUID as a normal authenticated user does not return the required 403 response when the target user does not exist; it returns 404 instead.
omissions.reasoning: In GET /api/v1/users/{user_id}, the code first loads the user and raises HTTPException(status_code=404, detail="The user with this id does not exist in the system") if no user is found. Only after existence is confirmed does it check whether the current non-superuser is requesting someone else's ID and raise 403 with detail "The user doesn't have enough privileges". Therefore, for the scenario's random UUID that is not the authenticated user's ID, the response will be 404 rather than the required 403 with the specified body.

omissions.description: Duplicate user registration is rejected with the wrong error detail message.
omissions.reasoning: The registration endpoint `/api/v1/users/signup` does reject an existing email with status 400, but it returns `detail="User with this email already exists"` instead of the required `detail="The user with this email already exists in the system"`.

omissions.description: POST /api/v1/users/signup does not reject a full_name of exactly 256 characters with a 422 validation error.
omissions.reasoning: The signup endpoint uses the UserRegister/UserCreate model, whose validate_full_name validator only raises an error when len(full_name) > 255. A 256-character full_name therefore fails validation and FastAPI returns 422, satisfying the requirement.
